predecessors.name: Bahmani Sultanate
predecessors.text: the Telangana lands of the Bahmani Sultanate around Golconda

predecessors.name: Bidar Sultanate
predecessors.text: the eastern lands that Cliopatria draws inside Bidar to 1518 and inside Golconda from 1519

successors.name: Mughal Empire
successors.text: the whole sultanate, with the Carnatic lands of 1642-1650, 'annexed into a province of the Mughal territories' (the Hyderabad Subah)

ledger.x: 1518-1519: Golconda takes the eastern lands of the Bahmani heartland, the strip that Cliopatria draws inside Bidar to 1518.
December 1518: Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk founds the Qutb Shahi sultanate of Golconda.

c. 1521: Golconda extends south and south-east over about 193 cells (lat 15.9-17.6 N, lon 77.8-82.3 E) that Cliopatria takes from Vijayanagara in 1521. The Quli Qutb Shah page names the land without years: 'Sultan Quli extended his rule by capturing forts at Warangal, Kondapalli, Eluru, and Rajamundry', the fort of…

c. 1572: Golconda's shape grows by about 37 cells in the east. 'Following the battle of Talikota in 1565, Ibrahim was able to expand his own kingdom' but no land or year is named; the date is Cliopatria's. The Gajapati page gives the end of Gajapati rule as 1541, so land in the east without a…

c. 1612: Golconda's shape grows by about 191 cells along the north-eastern coast, held by no Cliopatria state. The Muhammad Quli page (he died 11 January 1612) records no conquest, so the event is a bridge between Cliopatria's shapes. The Gajapati page (rule ends 1541) does not mention Rajahmundry, Kondavidu or the…

c. 1640: Golconda's shape grows by about 96 cells in the Carnatic interior (the Guntur-Palnadu side), held by no Cliopatria state; Cliopatria adds 123 cells in 1640 of which 27 lie inside the Nellore circle of the 1646 event. The Mir Jumla page dates only Mir Jumla's own conquests (April 1642 onwards) and says nothing…
April 1642: Golconda's general Mir Jumla invades the Carnatic.
1646: Mir Jumla invades the Kingdom of Chandragiri and takes Udayagiri.

c. 1656-1659: the northern frontier of Golconda passes to the Mughals. The Siege of Golconda page dates only the peace after Aurangzeb's 1656 siege ('the siege was withdrawn and a peace treaty established by Shah Jahan') and names no ceded land; 1659 is Cliopatria's year for the 56 cells. The Abdullah Qutb Shah page…
September 1687: the Qutb Shahi sultanate ends and becomes a Mughal province (the Hyderabad Subah).

wars.name: Battle of Talikota
wars.outcome: Victory of the Deccan sultanates on 23 January 1565; the Ibrahim Quli page says he was able to expand his kingdom afterwards but names no land or year.

wars.name: Golconda's Carnatic campaigns under Mir Jumla
wars.outcome: Golconda gains the Nellore plains (April 1642), Udayagiri and a tributary submission from Chandragiri (1646-April 1647), and Gandikota (1650); Mir Jumla later joins the Mughals.

wars.name: Siege of Gingee (1648)
wars.outcome: Gingee 'fell to the Adil Shahis' in 1648 (Mir Jumla page); Bijapur and Golconda forces laid siege together (Shahaji page, which dates the Bijapur campaign to 1648).

wars.name: Mughal siege of Golconda (1656)
wars.outcome: Aurangzeb 'besieged Golconda in 1656; the siege was withdrawn and a peace treaty established by Shah Jahan'; the page names no ceded land.

wars.name: Siege of Golconda
wars.outcome: Mughal victory after a siege of 28 January - 22 September 1687; Golconda is annexed and Abul Hasan Qutb Shah imprisoned at Daulatabad.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary survey or treaty line for Golconda; frontiers with Bijapur, Bidar, Vijayanagara's successors and the Mughals are Cliopatria's approximations.
